name: Squeeze-failure fade — failed downside break re-enters range (15m)
rationale: ECONOMIC MECHANISM: the untested economic sub-case of the squeeze. The inbox already trades squeeze->breakout (momentum AND reversion). Here we trade the squeeze breakout that FAILS on the first bar. bb_width at a multi-window floor (a coiled spring) followed by a downside poke that then re-enters the band = a false breakdown that trapped the breakdown/short crowd. Web evidence (2025 BB backtests) is explicit: naive band-touch/break is a coin-flip (PF~1.15) precisely BECAUSE false breaks dominate. So we FADE the failed break: when the breakdown crowd is trapped, their stop-outs (buy-to-cover) fuel the reversion back UP through the range. Entry (long): bb_width below a fitted floor (coiled spring present) AND range_position below a fitted floor (price poked to the lower band) AND rsi in washout (the down-poke overshot). The re-entry / failure is captured by holding for the snap-back. The other side is the breakout/breakdown algos (the most-cloned crypto template) that mechanically sell the band-break; we take the other side of their stop cascade. Distinct from squeeze-then-trend (which BUYS the confirmed break) — this requires the break to FAIL as the setup. Exit: range_position crosses up back into mid-band (snap-back complete) or stop/TP/time. DISCONFIRMER 1: if removing the squeeze pre-condition (fade ANY lower-band poke regardless of prior bb_width floor) works as well, the SQUEEZE isn't the edge — it's generic false-breakout fading and doesn't belong in the vol family. DISCONFIRMER 2: net of ~20bps round-trip at 15m the many small fades must clear; if per-trade edge < fees, trade count kills it.
catalyst: a coiled-spring squeeze whose downside break fails and traps the breakdown crowd
